questions.name: #322 The Antarctic and the Arctic
questions.en:
At the height of summer the Antarctic, tourist ships move gently around the coast.
Even 30 years ago such sights would have been unthinkable, but today people are willing to pay large sums of money to see the last real wilderness in the world.
In the Arctic, careless human exploitation ______ ______ ______ has damaged the fragile ecosystem.
Today concerned governments are trying to find ways to develop the region ______ caring for the very special natural environment.
  ______ the Antarctic is less accessible than the Arctic, it is still largely undamaged by humans, although holes in the ozone layer above the Antarctic ______ ______ ______ discovered.
Many people believe that one way to preserve the area is to make the whole region into a world park, with every form of exploitation internationally ______ .
whereas , have already been , in the future , is to be , while , Except , Because , in the past , banned , infested
questions.answer:
1. in
2. the
3. past
4. while
5. Because
6. have
7. already
8. been
9. banned
questions.full:
At the height of summer the Antarctic, tourist ships move gently around the coast.
Even 30 years ago such sights would have been unthinkable, but today people are willing to pay large sums of money to see the last real wilderness in the world.
In the Arctic, careless human exploitation ______ ______ ______ has damaged the fragile ecosystem.
Today concerned governments are trying to find ways to develop the region ______ caring for the very special natural environment.
  ______ the Antarctic is less accessible than the Arctic, it is still largely undamaged by humans, although holes in the ozone layer above the Antarctic ______ ______ ______ discovered.
Many people believe that one way to preserve the area is to make the whole region into a world park, with every form of exploitation internationally ______ .

whereas , have already been , in the future , is to be , while , Except , Because , in the past , banned , infested

答案:
1. in
2. the
3. past
4. while
5. Because
6. have
7. already
8. been
9. banned

sense_groups.english: At the height of summer the Antarctic, tourist ships move gently around the coast.
sense_groups.chinese: 在盛夏的南极，游船在海岸边缓缓行驶。

sense_groups.english: Even 30 years ago such sights would have been unthinkable, but today people are willing to pay large sums of money to see the last real wilderness in the world.
sense_groups.chinese: 即使在30年前，这样的景象也是难以想象的，但如今人们愿意花大价钱去看世界上最后的真正荒野。

sense_groups.english: In the Arctic, careless human exploitation in the past has damaged the fragile ecosystem.
sense_groups.chinese: 在北极，过去人类粗心的开发已经破坏了脆弱的生态系统。

sense_groups.english: Today concerned governments are trying to find ways to develop the region while caring for the very special natural environment.
sense_groups.chinese: 如今，忧心忡忡的政府正试图找到在开发该地区的同时保护其特殊自然环境的方法。

sense_groups.english: Because the Antarctic is less accessible than the Arctic, it is still largely undamaged by humans, although holes in the ozone layer above the Antarctic have already been discovered.
sense_groups.chinese: 由于南极比北极更难到达，它基本上仍未被人类破坏，尽管南极上空的臭氧层空洞已经被发现。

sense_groups.english: Many people believe that one way to preserve the area is to make the whole region into a world park, with every form of exploitation internationally banned.
sense_groups.chinese: 许多人认为保护该地区的一种方法是把整个区域变成一个世界公园，所有形式的开发都被国际禁止。

questions.name: #323 Houston
questions.en:
Houston is the fifth-largest metropolitan area in the United States and has an outsized ______ on the U.S. economy.
More than 90 percent of U.S. offshore oil and gas ______ takes place in the Texas Gulf Coast area, and the Houston region contains the largest ______ of energy, petrochemical, and refining industries in the United States.
Houston is home to 25 percent of the country's petroleum refining capability, 40 percent of the nation's capacity for downstream chemical production, and the fastest-growing liquefied natural gas industry in the nation.
pollution , impact , classification , production , concentration , impetus
questions.full:
Houston is the fifth-largest metropolitan area in the United States and has an outsized ______ on the U.S. economy.
More than 90 percent of U.S. offshore oil and gas ______ takes place in the Texas Gulf Coast area, and the Houston region contains the largest ______ of energy, petrochemical, and refining industries in the United States.
Houston is home to 25 percent of the country's petroleum refining capability, 40 percent of the nation's capacity for downstream chemical production, and the fastest-growing liquefied natural gas industry in the nation.

pollution , impact , classification , production , concentration , impetus

答案:
1. impact
2. production
3. concentration

sense_groups.english: Houston is the fifth-largest metropolitan area in the United States
sense_groups.chinese: 休斯顿是美国第五大都市区

sense_groups.english: and has an outsized impact on the U.S. economy.
sense_groups.chinese: 并对美国经济有着巨大的影响。

sense_groups.english: More than 90 percent of U.S. offshore oil and gas production takes place in the Texas Gulf Coast area,
sense_groups.chinese: 美国超过90%的离岸石油和天然气生产发生在德克萨斯州墨西哥湾沿岸地区，

sense_groups.english: and the Houston region contains the largest concentration of energy, petrochemical, and refining industries in the United States.
sense_groups.chinese: 而休斯顿地区拥有美国最大的能源、石化和炼油工业集中地。

sense_groups.english: Houston is home to 25 percent of the country's petroleum refining capability,
sense_groups.chinese: 休斯顿拥有全国25%的石油精炼能力，

sense_groups.english: 40 percent of the nation's capacity for downstream chemical production,
sense_groups.chinese: 全国40%的下游化工生产能力，

sense_groups.english: and the fastest-growing liquefied natural gas industry in the nation.
sense_groups.chinese: 以及全国增长最快的液化天然气产业。

questions.name: #324 Tree and City
questions.en:
A new report by environmental ______ The Nature Conservancy lays out how trees could pave the way to cleaner air and cooler cities.
Using ______ information on forest cover paired with air pollution data and population ______ for 245 cities, researchers found that trees have the biggest health ______ in densely populated, polluted cities like Delhi, Karachi and Dhaka.
The Conservancy and the C40 Cities Climate Leadership Group presented the findings of their global survey this week at the American Public Health Association meeting in Denver, Colorado.
geospatial , payoffs , retrospection , forecasts , layoffs , nonprofit , archaeological , defective
questions.full:
A new report by environmental ______ The Nature Conservancy lays out how trees could pave the way to cleaner air and cooler cities.
Using ______ information on forest cover paired with air pollution data and population ______ for 245 cities, researchers found that trees have the biggest health ______ in densely populated, polluted cities like Delhi, Karachi and Dhaka.
The Conservancy and the C40 Cities Climate Leadership Group presented the findings of their global survey this week at the American Public Health Association meeting in Denver, Colorado.

geospatial , payoffs , retrospection , forecasts , layoffs , nonprofit , archaeological , defective

答案:
1. nonprofit
2. geospatial
3. forecasts
4. payoffs

sense_groups.english: A new report by environmental nonprofit The Nature Conservancy
sense_groups.chinese: 一份由环保非营利组织大自然保护协会发布的新报告

sense_groups.english: lays out how trees could pave the way to cleaner air and cooler cities.
sense_groups.chinese: 阐述了树木如何能为更清洁的空气和更凉爽的城市铺平道路。

sense_groups.english: Using geospatial information on forest cover
sense_groups.chinese: 利用森林覆盖的地理空间信息

sense_groups.english: paired with air pollution data and population forecasts for 245 cities,
sense_groups.chinese: 结合245个城市的空气污染数据和人口预测，

sense_groups.english: researchers found that trees have the biggest health payoffs
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员发现，树木在人口密集、污染严重的城市中健康效益最大，

sense_groups.english: in densely populated, polluted cities like Delhi, Karachi and Dhaka.
sense_groups.chinese: 例如德里、卡拉奇和达卡。

sense_groups.english: The Conservancy and the C40 Cities Climate Leadership Group
sense_groups.chinese: 大自然保护协会和C40城市气候领导联盟

sense_groups.english: presented the findings of their global survey this week
sense_groups.chinese: 本周在科罗拉多州丹佛市举行的美国公共卫生协会会议上

sense_groups.english: at the American Public Health Association meeting in Denver, Colorado.
sense_groups.chinese: 展示了他们全球调查的结果。

questions.name: #325 Debtor
questions.en:
There isn't a financial director around who wouldn't like to ______ cash flow by ______ debtor days- in other words, get customers to ______ ______ faster.
In Europe's top 1,000 quoted companies, nearly one quarter of all invoices are unpaid ______ ______ ______ in time, according to recent research carried out by the ASF organization.
This means they are sitting on a total of 274 billion overdue debt.
Most of this is caused by poor collection practices.
According to Jan Porter, ASF's Managing Director, 'You can set up all the systems you want, you can insist on watertight contracts and payment terms, the government can even introduce late payment legislation, but there are always some debtors who fail to pay on time.
Once a payment is overdue, your first step is to talk to your debtor.
You should let them know the payment is late and try to find out if there is a dispute about the work, or if your debtor has financial problems.
  ______ ______ ______ , but Tim Vainio, a chartered accountant, believes that too many companies are afraid of losing a relationship, and that, before ______ ______ ______ , the focus should be on recovering as much money as possible, rather than on preserving a relationship.'
reproducing , accelerate , renew , pay up , check , reducing , accumulate , at any point , This is OK , It is unlikely , undertaking any action
questions.answer:
1. accelerate
2. reducing
3. pay
4. up
5. at
6. any
7. point
8. This
9. is
10. OK
11. undertaking
12. action
questions.full:
There isn't a financial director around who wouldn't like to ______ cash flow by ______ debtor days- in other words, get customers to ______ ______ faster.
In Europe's top 1,000 quoted companies, nearly one quarter of all invoices are unpaid ______ ______ ______ in time, according to recent research carried out by the ASF organization.
This means they are sitting on a total of 274 billion overdue debt.
Most of this is caused by poor collection practices.
According to Jan Porter, ASF's Managing Director, 'You can set up all the systems you want, you can insist on watertight contracts and payment terms, the government can even introduce late payment legislation, but there are always some debtors who fail to pay on time.
Once a payment is overdue, your first step is to talk to your debtor.
You should let them know the payment is late and try to find out if there is a dispute about the work, or if your debtor has financial problems.
  ______ ______ ______ , but Tim Vainio, a chartered accountant, believes that too many companies are afraid of losing a relationship, and that, before ______ ______ ______ , the focus should be on recovering as much money as possible, rather than on preserving a relationship.'

reproducing , accelerate , renew , pay up , check , reducing , accumulate , at any point , This is OK , It is unlikely , undertaking any action

答案:
1. accelerate
2. reducing
3. pay
4. up
5. at
6. any
7. point
8. This
9. is
10. OK
11. undertaking
12. action

sense_groups.english: There isn't a financial director around who wouldn't like to accelerate cash flow by reducing debtor days
sense_groups.chinese: 没有一个财务总监不想通过减少应收账款天数来加速现金流

sense_groups.english: - in other words, get customers to pay up faster.
sense_groups.chinese: 换句话说，就是让客户更快付款。

sense_groups.english: In Europe's top 1,000 quoted companies, nearly one quarter of all invoices are unpaid at any point in time,
sense_groups.chinese: 在欧洲排名前1000的上市公司中，近四分之一的发票在任何时候都未付款，

sense_groups.english: according to recent research carried out by the ASF organization.
sense_groups.chinese: 根据ASF组织最近进行的研究。

sense_groups.english: This means they are sitting on a total of 274 billion overdue debt.
sense_groups.chinese: 这意味着他们坐拥总计2740亿的逾期债务。

sense_groups.english: Most of this is caused by poor collection practices.
sense_groups.chinese: 这主要是由糟糕的收款做法造成的。

sense_groups.english: According to Jan Porter, ASF's Managing Director, 'You can set up all the systems you want,
sense_groups.chinese: ASF董事总经理Jan Porter表示：“你可以建立所有你想要的系统，

sense_groups.english: you can insist on watertight contracts and payment terms,
sense_groups.chinese: 你可以坚持无懈可击的合同和付款条款，

sense_groups.english: the government can even introduce late payment legislation,
sense_groups.chinese: 政府甚至可以出台逾期付款立法，

sense_groups.english: but there are always some debtors who fail to pay on time.
sense_groups.chinese: 但总有一些债务人未能按时付款。

sense_groups.english: Once a payment is overdue, your first step is to talk to your debtor.
sense_groups.chinese: 一旦付款逾期，你的第一步是与债务人沟通。

sense_groups.english: You should let them know the payment is late and try to find out if there is a dispute about the work,
sense_groups.chinese: 你应该让他们知道付款已逾期，并尝试查明是否存在工作上的争议，

sense_groups.english: or if your debtor has financial problems.
sense_groups.chinese: 或者你的债务人是否有财务问题。

sense_groups.english: This is OK, but Tim Vainio, a chartered accountant, believes that too many companies are afraid of losing a relationship,
sense_groups.chinese: 这没问题，但特许会计师Tim Vainio认为，太多公司害怕失去关系，

sense_groups.english: and that, before undertaking any action, the focus should be on recovering as much money as possible, rather than on preserving a relationship.'
sense_groups.chinese: 并且在采取任何行动之前，重点应该放在尽可能多地收回资金上，而不是维护关系。

questions.name: #326 The Press
questions.en:
Throughout its history, one of the strengths of the Press has been the diversity of the Press's list.
The Press has also distinguished itself with its strong list in social work, publishing texts that have been ______ adopted in courses and are used by professionals in the field.
Through its European Perspectives ______ and the publication of the Wellek Library Lectures, the Press has published a range of innovative and ______ scholars.
Other notable lecture series published by Columbia University Press include The Leonard Hastings Schoff Memorial Lectures and The Bampton Lectures in America.
series , supporting , episodes , leading , thoroughly , widely
questions.full:
Throughout its history, one of the strengths of the Press has been the diversity of the Press's list.
The Press has also distinguished itself with its strong list in social work, publishing texts that have been ______ adopted in courses and are used by professionals in the field.
Through its European Perspectives ______ and the publication of the Wellek Library Lectures, the Press has published a range of innovative and ______ scholars.
Other notable lecture series published by Columbia University Press include The Leonard Hastings Schoff Memorial Lectures and The Bampton Lectures in America.

series , supporting , episodes , leading , thoroughly , widely

答案:
1. widely
2. series
3. leading

sense_groups.english: Throughout its history, one of the strengths of the Press has been the diversity of the Press's list.
sense_groups.chinese: 纵观其历史，出版社的优势之一是其书目的多样性。

sense_groups.english: The Press has also distinguished itself with its strong list in social work, publishing texts that have been widely adopted in courses and are used by professionals in the field.

questions.name: #339 Merchant Navies
questions.en:

That race was to make the most luxurious and fastest ocean liners and it started with the Kaiser Wilhelm der Grosse, the first of fourteen four-stackers built between 1897 and 1921.
The large vessels that followed each tried to outdo the previous one in terms of size and interior design.

Through Kronprinzessin Cecilie, Mauretania, Aquitania, Olympic, Titanic, Imperator, Vaterland, Ile de France, and Paris, the development and design of the ships grew grander and more luxurious.
The process continued into the 1930s, with the Empress of Britain and the fabulously Art Deco Normandie, the finest and most expensive liner ever built, and designed to be a showcase for all that was France, as well as with the Queen Mary, a rather more traditional vessel, but one, ______ , which pushed the boundaries of design away from the traditional country house look of the Edwardian era.
Each new vessel brought with it the finest of interiors, from the plush and palatial to the modern look of the time.
Even today, the influence of these floating ______ can still be seen in vessels such as Cunard's Queen Mary 2 and the multitude of new cruise vessels, all vying for the public's interest and affection.
The large liners were truly floating palaces, and here, William H. Miller brings together a collection of fabulous images of the finest ships ever built, showcasing the style and elegance of a time when 'getting there was half the fun'.

questions.full:

questions.full:
One of the best studied applications of plasmonic materials is sensors for ______ chemical and biological agents.
In one approach, researchers coat a plasmonic nanomaterial with a substance that ______ to a molecule of interest--say, a bacterial toxin.
In the absence of the toxin, light shining on the material is ______ at a specific angle.
But if the toxin is present, it will alter the frequency of the surface plasmon and, thus consequently, the angle of the reflected light.
This effect can be measured with great accuracy, ______ even trace amounts of the toxin to be detected and measured.

rejected , sorting , enabling , reemitted , revolves , detecting , binds

答案:
1. detecting
2. binds
3. reemitted
4. enabling

sense_groups.english: One of the best studied applications of plasmonic materials is sensors for detecting chemical and biological agents.
sense_groups.chinese: 等离子体材料研究最充分的应用之一是用于检测化学和生物制剂的传感器。

sense_groups.english: In one approach, researchers coat a plasmonic nanomaterial with a substance that binds to a molecule of interest--say, a bacterial toxin.
sense_groups.chinese: 在一种方法中，研究人员在等离子体纳米材料上涂覆一种物质，这种物质会与目标分子（比如细菌毒素）结合。

sense_groups.chinese: 在没有毒素的情况下，照射在材料上的光会以特定角度重新发射。

sense_groups.english: But if the toxin is present, it will alter the frequency of the surface plasmon and, thus consequently, the angle of the reflected light.
sense_groups.chinese: 但如果毒素存在，它会改变表面等离子体的频率，从而改变反射光的角度。

sense_groups.english: This effect can be measured with great accuracy, enabling even trace amounts of the toxin to be detected and measured.
sense_groups.chinese: 这种效应可以非常精确地测量，从而能够检测和测量即使是微量的毒素。

questions.full:
Sydney is becoming effective in making the best of its limited available unconstrained land.
Sydney is suitable for integrating suitable business, office, residential, retail and other development in accessible locations so as to maximize public transport ______ and encourage walking and cycling.
Also this city can reduce the ______ of land for housing and associated urban development on the urban fringe.
For the proposed mixed business, mixed use and business park areas, there was no employment data available for ______ areas.
It is also concluded that lack of housing supply will affect ______ in Sydney.

consumption , patronage , comparable , alternative , expectation , affordability , contemporary

2. consumption
3. comparable
4. affordability

sense_groups.english: Sydney is becoming effective in making the best of its limited available unconstrained land.
sense_groups.chinese: 悉尼正有效地利用其有限的可用未开发土地。

sense_groups.english: Sydney is suitable for integrating suitable business, office, residential, retail and other development in accessible locations
sense_groups.chinese: 悉尼适合在交通便利的地点整合商业、办公、住宅、零售等开发项目，

sense_groups.english: so as to maximize public transport patronage and encourage walking and cycling.
sense_groups.chinese: 以最大化公共交通的客流量，并鼓励步行和骑行。

sense_groups.english: Also this city can reduce the consumption of land for housing and associated urban development on the urban fringe.
sense_groups.chinese: 此外，该城市可以减少城市边缘地带用于住房及相关城市开发的土地消耗。

sense_groups.chinese: 对于拟议的混合商业、混合用途和商业园区区域，没有可比区域的就业数据。

sense_groups.english: It is also concluded that lack of housing supply will affect affordability in Sydney.
sense_groups.chinese: 研究还得出结论，住房供应不足将影响悉尼的住房可负担性。

questions.name: #394 Statistical Theory
questions.en:

Endangered species of fish and other wildlife are protected through regulations and laws that react to statistical estimates of changing population sizes.

through , using , initiated , changed , though , entailing , such
questions.full:
Social reforms are normally ______ as a result of statistical analyses of factors such as crime rates and poverty levels etc. Large-scale population can result from projections devised by statisticians.
Manufacturers can provide better products at lower costs by ______ statistical control tools, ______ as control charts.
Diseases are controlled through analyses designed to anticipate epidemics.
Endangered species of fish and other wildlife are protected through regulations and laws that react to statistical estimates of changing population sizes.
And, ______ statistical analysis of fatality rates, legislators can better justify laws, such as those governing air pollution, auto inspections, seat belt and airbag use, and drunk driving.

through , using , initiated , changed , though , entailing , such

答案:
1. initiated
2. using
3. such
4. through

sense_groups.english: Social reforms are normally initiated as a result of statistical analyses of factors such as crime rates and poverty levels etc.
sense_groups.chinese: 社会改革通常是由对犯罪率、贫困水平等因素的统计分析引发的。

sense_groups.english: Large-scale population can result from projections devised by statisticians.
sense_groups.chinese: 大规模人口变化可能源于统计学家设计的预测。

sense_groups.english: Manufacturers can provide better products at lower costs by using statistical control tools, such as control charts.
sense_groups.chinese: 制造商可以通过使用统计控制工具（如控制图）以更低的成本提供更好的产品。

sense_groups.english: Diseases are controlled through analyses designed to anticipate epidemics.
sense_groups.chinese: 疾病通过旨在预测流行病的分析得到控制。

sense_groups.english: Endangered species of fish and other wildlife are protected through regulations and laws that react to statistical estimates of changing population sizes.
sense_groups.chinese: 濒危鱼类和其他野生动物通过针对种群规模变化的统计估计而制定的法规和法律得到保护。

sense_groups.english: And, through statistical analysis of fatality rates, legislators can better justify laws, such as those governing air pollution, auto inspections, seat belt and airbag use, and drunk driving.
sense_groups.chinese: 并且，通过对死亡率的统计分析，立法者可以更好地为法律辩护，例如那些关于空气污染、汽车检查、安全带和安全气囊使用以及酒驾的法律。

questions.name: #398 Effective Leaders

After extensive interviews with more than 50 of them, the author discovered that most are ______ thinkers -that is, they can hold in their heads two opposing ideas at once and then come up with a new idea that contains elements of ______ but is superior to both.

questions.full:

Roger Martin says this focus is misplaced, because moves that work in one context may make little sense in another.
A more productive, though more difficult, approach is to look at how such leaders ______ .
After extensive interviews with more than 50 of them, the author discovered that most are ______ thinkers -that is, they can hold in their heads two opposing ideas at once and then come up with a new idea that contains elements of ______ but is superior to both.

integrative , disdain , emulate , either , each , appoint , show , apply , think , communal

答案:

2. emulate
3. think
4. integrative

sense_groups.english: In search of lessons to apply in our own careers,
sense_groups.chinese: 为了寻找可以应用到我们自己职业生涯中的经验教训，

sense_groups.chinese: 我们常常试图模仿高效领导者的做法。

questions.name: #399 Melting Ice

questions.full:

Even ______ the rest of the planet was warming ______ ,the North Atlantic region remained in a cold period for 1300 years.

sense_groups.chinese: 大约8000年前发生了同样的事情，

sense_groups.chinese: 当时冷却持续了大约一百年，

sense_groups.chinese: 即使是北大西洋短暂的冷却期

questions.name: #439 Self-defeating Habits
questions.en:
Don't allow yourself to slip into self-defeating habits, such as procrastinating.
Try to keep a ______ going in your study.
Scatter blocks of study with short breaks to limit fatigue.
If you study solidly for a couple of hours, make sure you give yourself fifteen minutes or so before you start up again.
Think positively about yourself and your situation.
Challenge the negative thoughts that ______ into your mind and cause you unnecessary stress at times, such as 'I'm going to fail', 'I'll end up blowing my future, my chance of getting a career'.
You don't have any need to think catastrophically, it's not achieving anything.
In fact, it's doing you a lot more harm than good, because it's distracting you away from what you need to do.
Learn to become more relaxed in your daily life.
There are simple techniques, such as breathing exercises and ______ muscular relaxation exercises, as well as guided imagery, which can help you to feel calmer, and more focused.
The Macquarie University Counsellors can help you with these techniques.
Some do relaxation tapes for students.
creep , progressive , status , escape , evanescent , momentum
questions.full:
Don't allow yourself to slip into self-defeating habits, such as procrastinating.
Try to keep a ______ going in your study.
Scatter blocks of study with short breaks to limit fatigue.
If you study solidly for a couple of hours, make sure you give yourself fifteen minutes or so before you start up again.

In fact, it's doing you a lot more harm than good, because it's distracting you away from what you need to do.

2. creep

sense_groups.english: Don't allow yourself to slip into self-defeating habits, such as procrastinating.
sense_groups.chinese: 不要让自己陷入自我挫败的习惯，比如拖延。

sense_groups.english: Try to keep a momentum going in your study.
sense_groups.chinese: 试着在学习中保持动力。

sense_groups.english: Scatter blocks of study with short breaks to limit fatigue.
sense_groups.chinese: 在学习时段中穿插短暂休息以限制疲劳。

sense_groups.english: If you study solidly for a couple of hours, make sure you give yourself fifteen minutes or so before you start up again.
sense_groups.chinese: 如果你连续学习几个小时，确保在重新开始前给自己十五分钟左右的时间。

sense_groups.english: Think positively about yourself and your situation.
sense_groups.chinese: 积极看待自己和自己的处境。

sense_groups.english: Challenge the negative thoughts that creep into your mind and cause you unnecessary stress at times, such as 'I'm going to fail', 'I'll end up blowing my future, my chance of getting a career'.
sense_groups.chinese: 挑战那些潜入你脑海并有时造成不必要压力的消极想法，比如‘我会失败’、‘我会毁掉我的未来、我的职业机会’。

sense_groups.english: You don't have any need to think catastrophically, it's not achieving anything.
sense_groups.chinese: 你完全没有必要灾难化思考，这毫无益处。

sense_groups.english: In fact, it's doing you a lot more harm than good, because it's distracting you away from what you need to do.
sense_groups.chinese: 事实上，它对你弊大于利，因为它让你分心，远离你需要做的事情。

sense_groups.english: Learn to become more relaxed in your daily life.

questions.name: #441 City Cleaner
questions.en:
Rather than ______ at the next beetle or wasp in your way, you might want to thank them-- for helping to keep city streets clean.
Researchers from North Carolina State University working in New York City found that hungry urban arthropods play a significant role in the disposal of trash.
For example, in a small section of Manhattan called the Broadway/West Street corridor, insects consume the equivalent of 60,000 hot dogs a year that would otherwise be lying in the street.
And that's ______ the bugs stop chowing down in winter.
To assess how much ______ food bugs got rid of, the researchers placed ______ amounts of hot dogs, potato chips and cookies at 21 park sites and 24 street medians.
Contrary to their prediction, location played an even bigger role in garbage ______ than biodiversity did--insects gobbled up two to three times more food in the street medians than they did in the parks.
The study appears in the journal Global Change Biology.
If all that garbage disposal still does not make you an arthropod admirer, then consider this: by competing with larger pests for resources, insects help keep rat populations down.
There's some food for ______ .
discarded , measured , assuming , thought , cringing , engagement , preparing , consumption
questions.answer:
1. cringing
2. assuming
3. discarded
4. measured
5. consumption
6. thought
questions.full:
Rather than ______ at the next beetle or wasp in your way, you might want to thank them-- for helping to keep city streets clean.
Researchers from North Carolina State University working in New York City found that hungry urban arthropods play a significant role in the disposal of trash.
For example, in a small section of Manhattan called the Broadway/West Street corridor, insects consume the equivalent of 60,000 hot dogs a year that would otherwise be lying in the street.
And that's ______ the bugs stop chowing down in winter.
To assess how much ______ food bugs got rid of, the researchers placed ______ amounts of hot dogs, potato chips and cookies at 21 park sites and 24 street medians.
Contrary to their prediction, location played an even bigger role in garbage ______ than biodiversity did--insects gobbled up two to three times more food in the street medians than they did in the parks.
The study appears in the journal Global Change Biology.
If all that garbage disposal still does not make you an arthropod admirer, then consider this: by competing with larger pests for resources, insects help keep rat populations down.
There's some food for ______ .

discarded , measured , assuming , thought , cringing , engagement , preparing , consumption

答案:
1. cringing
2. assuming
3. discarded
4. measured
5. consumption
6. thought

sense_groups.english: Rather than cringing at the next beetle or wasp in your way,
sense_groups.chinese: 与其对下一只挡路的甲虫或黄蜂感到畏缩，

sense_groups.english: you might want to thank them--
sense_groups.chinese: 你或许该感谢它们——

sense_groups.english: for helping to keep city streets clean.
sense_groups.chinese: 因为它们帮助保持城市街道清洁。

sense_groups.english: Researchers from North Carolina State University working in New York City found
sense_groups.chinese: 北卡罗来纳州立大学在纽约市工作的研究人员发现，

sense_groups.english: that hungry urban arthropods play a significant role in the disposal of trash.
sense_groups.chinese: 饥饿的城市节肢动物在垃圾处理中扮演着重要角色。

sense_groups.english: For example, in a small section of Manhattan called the Broadway/West Street corridor,
sense_groups.chinese: 例如，在曼哈顿一个名为百老汇/西街走廊的小区域，

sense_groups.english: insects consume the equivalent of 60,000 hot dogs a year
sense_groups.chinese: 昆虫每年消耗相当于6万个热狗的食物，

sense_groups.english: that would otherwise be lying in the street.
sense_groups.chinese: 否则这些食物就会躺在街上。

sense_groups.english: And that's assuming the bugs stop chowing down in winter.
sense_groups.chinese: 而且这还是假设虫子们在冬天停止大吃大喝的情况下。

sense_groups.english: To assess how much discarded food bugs got rid of,
sense_groups.chinese: 为了评估虫子清除了多少丢弃的食物，

sense_groups.english: the researchers placed measured amounts of hot dogs, potato chips and cookies
sense_groups.chinese: 研究人员将测量好的热狗、薯片和饼干，

sense_groups.english: at 21 park sites and 24 street medians.
sense_groups.chinese: 放置在21个公园地点和24个街道中央隔离带上。

sense_groups.english: Contrary to their prediction,
sense_groups.chinese: 与他们的预测相反，

sense_groups.english: location played an even bigger role in garbage consumption than biodiversity did--
sense_groups.chinese: 地点在垃圾消耗中的作用甚至比生物多样性更大——

sense_groups.english: insects gobbled up two to three times more food in the street medians than they did in the parks.
sense_groups.chinese: 昆虫在街道中央隔离带上吃掉的食物是公园里的两到三倍。

sense_groups.english: The study appears in the journal Global Change Biology.
sense_groups.chinese: 这项研究发表在《全球变化生物学》期刊上。

sense_groups.english: If all that garbage disposal still does not make you an arthropod admirer,
sense_groups.chinese: 如果所有这些垃圾处理还不能让你成为节肢动物的崇拜者，

sense_groups.english: then consider this:
sense_groups.chinese: 那么考虑一下这一点：

sense_groups.english: by competing with larger pests for resources,
sense_groups.chinese: 通过与更大的害虫竞争资源，

sense_groups.english: insects help keep rat populations down.
sense_groups.chinese: 昆虫有助于控制老鼠的数量。

sense_groups.english: There's some food for thought.
sense_groups.chinese: 这值得深思。

questions.name: #442 Customer Service
questions.en:
Promoting good customer service must start at the ______ .
If management doesn't realize how important this aspect of their business is, they will be at an ______ disadvantage in their industry.
Good customer response ______ to loyal customers, which are the ______ of any successful business.
No matter how much money you invest in your marketing, if you don't have the fundamental elements of your business right, it's wasted money.
top , cornerstone , instant , cost , equates , incomplete , equalizes
questions.full:
Promoting good customer service must start at the ______ .
If management doesn't realize how important this aspect of their business is, they will be at an ______ disadvantage in their industry.
Good customer response ______ to loyal customers, which are the ______ of any successful business.
No matter how much money you invest in your marketing, if you don't have the fundamental elements of your business right, it's wasted money.

top , cornerstone , instant , cost , equates , incomplete , equalizes

答案:
1. top
2. instant
3. equates
4. cornerstone

sense_groups.english: Promoting good customer service must start at the top.
sense_groups.chinese: 推广良好的客户服务必须从高层开始。

sense_groups.english: If management doesn't realize how important this aspect of their business is,
sense_groups.chinese: 如果管理层没有意识到这个方面对他们业务的重要性，

sense_groups.english: they will be at an instant disadvantage in their industry.
sense_groups.chinese: 他们将在行业中立即处于劣势。

sense_groups.english: Good customer response equates to loyal customers,
sense_groups.chinese: 良好的客户回应等同于忠诚的客户，

sense_groups.english: which are the cornerstone of any successful business.
sense_groups.chinese: 而忠诚的客户是任何成功企业的基石。

sense_groups.english: No matter how much money you invest in your marketing,
sense_groups.chinese: 无论你在市场营销上投入多少钱，

sense_groups.english: if you don't have the fundamental elements of your business right,
sense_groups.chinese: 如果你没有把业务的基本要素做好，

sense_groups.english: it's wasted money.
sense_groups.chinese: 那都是浪费钱。

questions.name: #443 Time Measuring
questions.en:
According to archaeological evidence, at least 5,000 years ago, and long before the ______ of the Roman Empire, the Babylonians began to measure time, introducing calendars to co-ordinate communal activities, to plan the ______ of goods and, in particular, to regulate planting and harvesting.
They based their ______ on three natural cycles: the solar day, marked by the successive periods of light and darkness as the earth rotates on its ______ ; the lunar month, following the phases of the moon as it orbits the earth; and the solar year, defined by the changing seasons that accompany our planet's revolution around the sun.
shipment , calendars , axis , advent , claim , pitch
questions.full:
According to archaeological evidence, at least 5,000 years ago, and long before the ______ of the Roman Empire, the Babylonians began to measure time, introducing calendars to co-ordinate communal activities, to plan the ______ of goods and, in particular, to regulate planting and harvesting.
They based their ______ on three natural cycles: the solar day, marked by the successive periods of light and darkness as the earth rotates on its ______ ; the lunar month, following the phases of the moon as it orbits the earth; and the solar year, defined by the changing seasons that accompany our planet's revolution around the sun.

shipment , calendars , axis , advent , claim , pitch

答案:
1. advent
2. shipment
3. calendars
4. axis

sense_groups.english: According to archaeological evidence, at least 5,000 years ago, and long before the advent of the Roman Empire,
sense_groups.chinese: 根据考古证据，至少在5000年前，远在罗马帝国出现之前，

sense_groups.english: the Babylonians began to measure time, introducing calendars to co-ordinate communal activities,
sense_groups.chinese: 巴比伦人就开始测量时间，引入日历以协调公共活动，

sense_groups.english: to plan the shipment of goods and, in particular, to regulate planting and harvesting.
sense_groups.chinese: 规划货物的运输，特别是调节种植和收获。

sense_groups.english: They based their calendars on three natural cycles:
sense_groups.chinese: 他们的历法基于三个自然周期：

sense_groups.english: the solar day, marked by the successive periods of light and darkness as the earth rotates on its axis;
sense_groups.chinese: 太阳日，由地球绕其自转轴旋转时交替的光明和黑暗时期标记；

sense_groups.english: the lunar month, following the phases of the moon as it orbits the earth;
sense_groups.chinese: 太阴月，遵循月球绕地球公转时的相位变化；

sense_groups.english: and the solar year, defined by the changing seasons that accompany our planet's revolution around the sun.
sense_groups.chinese: 以及太阳年，由伴随地球绕太阳公转的季节变化所定义。

questions.name: #459 Flower Color
questions.en:
A flower's colour, however, isn't a full-proof guide to a good lunch.
That's because the colour can change depending on the angle at which sunlight hits its petals.
A yellow flower, for example, may look somewhat blue from one angle and red from another.
Scientists call this kind of colour change iridescence.
'It's the same ______ that makes a rainbow appear in a soap bubble or on a CD,' says Beverley Glover.
She studies plants at the University of Cambridge in England.
In 2009, Glover and her colleagues showed that even when petals look ______ , bees can still tell which flowers likely hold food.
But she and others noticed something odd about iridescence.
It's not quite as flashy in plants as in other life forms, Glover says.
The backs of jewel, beetles, or the wings of certain butterflies, for instance, shine and shimmer a lot more.
The researchers tested their hypothesis in the lab.
They trained a group of bees to associate fake purple flowers with getting more nectar.
Then the team tested the bees.
They added non-shimmery ______ flowers with purple-blue and purple-red hues to the bees' flight path.
The bees passed the test, ignoring flowers that weren't perfectly purple.
Second group of bees was trained to drink from fully flashy, 'perfectly iridescent' purple flowers.
But when the team added perfectly iridescent flowers in different hues, the insects checked them for nectar, too.
A third group of bees, however, had no problem finding the right flowers when the petals had only a little bit of bling.
These bees were trained to drink from ' ______ iridescent' purple flowers.
When the team added imperfectly iridescent flowers in different hues, the bees weren't confused at all.
'They could still clearly identify the purple flowers as the good ones,' Glover says.
That means imperfect iridescence is best for bees.

questions.name: #460 SARS
questions.en:
Scientists around the world are racing to learn how to rapidly diagnose, treat and stop the spread of a new, deadly disease.
SARS -- Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome -- was detected for the first time in February 2003 in Hanoi, and since then has infected more than 1,600 people in 15 countries, killing 63.
At this ______ , there are more questions than answers surrounding the disease.
Symptoms start with a fever over 100.4 degrees F, chills, headache or body aches.
Within a week, the patient has a dry cough, which might ______ to shortness of breath.
In 10% to 20% of cases, patients require mechanical ventilation to breathe.
About 3.5% die from the disease.
Symptoms ______ begin in two to seven days, but some reports suggest it might take as long as 10 days.
Scientists are close to ______ a lab test to diagnose SARS.
In the meantime, it is diagnosed by its symptoms.
There is no evidence that antibiotics or anti-viral medicines help, so doctors can offer only supportive care.
Patients with SARS are kept in isolation to reduce the risk of transmission.
Scientists aren't sure yet, but some researchers think it's a newly discovered coronavirus, the family of viruses that cause some common colds.
Most cases appear to have been passed through droplets expelled when infected patients cough or sneeze.
Family members of infected people and medical workers who care for them have been most likely to contract the illness.
But recent developments in Hong Kong suggest that the disease might spread through air, or that the virus might linger for two to three hours on doorknobs or other ______ .
Health experts say it is unlikely, though, that sharing an elevator briefly with an infected person would be enough to pass the virus.
contents , cost , generally , exclusively , surfaces , quitting , point , revive , developing , progress
questions.full:
Scientists around the world are racing to learn how to rapidly diagnose, treat and stop the spread of a new, deadly disease.
SARS -- Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome -- was detected for the first time in February 2003 in Hanoi, and since then has infected more than 1,600 people in 15 countries, killing 63.

2. progress

4. developing

sense_groups.english: Scientists around the world are racing to learn how to rapidly diagnose, treat and stop the spread of a new, deadly disease.
sense_groups.chinese: 世界各地的科学家正在竞相学习如何快速诊断、治疗和阻止一种新的致命疾病的传播。

sense_groups.english: SARS -- Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome -- was detected for the first time in February 2003 in Hanoi, and since then has infected more than 1,600 people in 15 countries, killing 63.
sense_groups.chinese: SARS——严重急性呼吸综合征——于2003年2月在河内首次被发现，此后已在15个国家感染了1600多人，其中63人死亡。

sense_groups.english: At this point, there are more questions than answers surrounding the disease.
sense_groups.chinese: 目前，围绕这种疾病的问题多于答案。

sense_groups.english: Symptoms start with a fever over 100.4 degrees F, chills, headache or body aches.
sense_groups.chinese: 症状开始于超过100.4华氏度的发烧、寒战、头痛或身体疼痛。

sense_groups.english: Within a week, the patient has a dry cough, which might progress to shortness of breath.
sense_groups.chinese: 一周内，患者出现干咳，可能发展为呼吸急促。

sense_groups.english: In 10% to 20% of cases, patients require mechanical ventilation to breathe.
sense_groups.chinese: 在10%到20%的病例中，患者需要机械通气来呼吸。

sense_groups.english: About 3.5% die from the disease.
sense_groups.chinese: 大约3.5%的患者死于该病。

sense_groups.english: Symptoms generally begin in two to seven days, but some reports suggest it might take as long as 10 days.
sense_groups.chinese: 症状通常在2到7天内出现，但一些报告表明可能需要长达10天。

sense_groups.english: Scientists are close to developing a lab test to diagnose SARS.
sense_groups.chinese: 科学家们接近开发出一种实验室检测方法来诊断SARS。

sense_groups.english: In the meantime, it is diagnosed by its symptoms.
sense_groups.chinese: 与此同时，它是通过症状来诊断的。

sense_groups.english: There is no evidence that antibiotics or anti-viral medicines help, so doctors can offer only supportive care.
sense_groups.chinese: 没有证据表明抗生素或抗病毒药物有效，因此医生只能提供支持性护理。

sense_groups.english: Patients with SARS are kept in isolation to reduce the risk of transmission.
sense_groups.chinese: SARS患者被隔离以减少传播风险。

sense_groups.english: Scientists aren't sure yet, but some researchers think it's a newly discovered coronavirus, the family of viruses that cause some common colds.
sense_groups.chinese: 科学家们还不确定，但一些研究人员认为这是一种新发现的冠状病毒，属于引起一些普通感冒的病毒家族。

sense_groups.english: Most cases appear to have been passed through droplets expelled when infected patients cough or sneeze.
sense_groups.chinese: 大多数病例似乎是通过感染患者咳嗽或打喷嚏时排出的飞沫传播的。

sense_groups.english: Family members of infected people and medical workers who care for them have been most likely to contract the illness.
sense_groups.chinese: 感染者的家人和照顾他们的医护人员最有可能感染这种疾病。

sense_groups.english: But recent developments in Hong Kong suggest that the disease might spread through air, or that the virus might linger for two to three hours on doorknobs or other surfaces.
sense_groups.chinese: 但香港最近的事态发展表明，这种疾病可能通过空气传播，或者病毒可能在门把手或其他表面停留两到三个小时。

sense_groups.english: Health experts say it is unlikely, though, that sharing an elevator briefly with an infected person would be enough to pass the virus.
sense_groups.chinese: 不过，健康专家表示，与感染者短暂共乘电梯不太可能传播病毒。

questions.name: #465 Utopias
questions.en:

And in the 20th century there was Le Corbusier's Radiant City in which, if you weren't in a car or didn't have one, life would have been a nightmare.
Also in the 20th century; another famous architect, Frank Lloyd Wright, ______ up a perfect city that got no further than the drawing-board.
Wright believed that what was wrong with modern cities was, in his words, rent.
Ideas, land, even money itself, had to be paid for.
He saw this as a form of slavery and believed that modern city dwellers had no sense of themselves as productive individuals.
Thus, Wright's city was to be made up of numerous individual homesteads, and the houses themselves were to be simple, functional and in ______ with the environment.
Everyone would own enough land to grow food for himself and his family.
No outsiders would be allowed to come between the citizen and what he produced, or to exploit both for money.

sense_groups.english: Many Utopias have been dreamed up through the ages.
sense_groups.chinese: 许多乌托邦在历史上被构想出来。

sense_groups.english: From Plato's Republic to Thomas More's Utopia and beyond,
sense_groups.chinese: 从柏拉图的《理想国》到托马斯·莫尔的《乌托邦》及更远，

sense_groups.english: serious thinkers have envisioned societies where people live in peace and harmony.
sense_groups.chinese: 严肃的思想家们设想了人们和平和谐生活的社会。

sense_groups.english: Most of these imaginary worlds have things in common:
sense_groups.chinese: 这些想象中的世界大多有共同点：

sense_groups.english: everybody is equal and plays a part in the running of the society;
sense_groups.chinese: 人人平等，并在社会运行中发挥作用；

sense_groups.english: nobody goes without the essentials of life;
sense_groups.chinese: 没有人缺少生活必需品；

sense_groups.english: people live mostly off the land;

sense_groups.chinese: 在那里，如果你不在车里或没有车，

sense_groups.chinese: 生活将是一场噩梦。

sense_groups.english: Also in the 20th century; another famous architect, Frank Lloyd Wright,
sense_groups.chinese: 同样在20世纪，另一位著名建筑师弗兰克·劳埃德·赖特，

sense_groups.english: dreamed up a perfect city that got no further than the drawing-board.
sense_groups.chinese: 构想了一个完美的城市，但只停留在图纸上。

sense_groups.chinese: 赖特认为，用他的话来说，现代城市的问题在于租金。

sense_groups.english: Ideas, land, even money itself, had to be paid for.
sense_groups.chinese: 思想、土地，甚至金钱本身，都必须付费。

sense_groups.english: He saw this as a form of slavery
sense_groups.chinese: 他认为这是一种奴役形式，

sense_groups.english: and believed that modern city dwellers had no sense of themselves as productive individuals.
sense_groups.chinese: 并认为现代城市居民没有意识到自己是生产性个体。

sense_groups.english: Thus, Wright's city was to be made up of numerous individual homesteads,
sense_groups.chinese: 因此，赖特的城市将由众多独立的家庭农场组成，

sense_groups.english: and the houses themselves were to be simple, functional and in harmony with the environment.
sense_groups.chinese: 房屋本身要简单、实用，并与环境和谐。

sense_groups.english: Everyone would own enough land to grow food for himself and his family.
sense_groups.chinese: 每个人都将拥有足够的土地为自己和家人种植食物。

sense_groups.english: No outsiders would be allowed to come between the citizen and what he produced,
sense_groups.chinese: 不允许外人介入公民与其生产物之间，

sense_groups.english: or to exploit both for money.
sense_groups.chinese: 或为了金钱剥削两者。

sense_groups.english: Goods and services would all be exchanged,
sense_groups.chinese: 商品和服务都将被交换，

sense_groups.english: not bought and sold for profit.
sense_groups.chinese: 而不是为了利润买卖。

questions.full:
The speed of sound (otherwise known as Mach 1) varies with temperature.

As the altitude increases, the temperature and speed of sound ______ decrease until about 36,000 feet, after which the temperature ______ steady until about 60,000 feet.

Because of the ______ , it is possible for an airplane flying supersonic at high altitude to be slower than a subsonic flight at sea level.
The transonic band (the 'sound barrier‘) extends ______ around Mach 0.8 — when the first supersonic shock waves form on the wing — to Mach 1.2, when the entire wing has gone supersonic.

via , towards , both , from , variation , differences , either, remains, tends

sense_groups.english: The speed of sound (otherwise known as Mach 1) varies with temperature.
sense_groups.chinese: 声速（也称为马赫1）随温度变化。

sense_groups.english: At sea level on a 'standard day', the temperature is 59°F, and Mach 1 is approximately 761 mph.
sense_groups.chinese: 在海平面标准日，温度为59华氏度，马赫1约为761英里/小时。

sense_groups.english: As the altitude increases, the temperature and speed of sound both decrease until about 36,000 feet, after which the temperature remains steady until about 60,000 feet.
sense_groups.chinese: 随着海拔升高，温度和声速都下降，直到约36,000英尺，之后温度保持稳定直到约60,000英尺。

sense_groups.english: Within that 36,000 – 60,000 foot range, Mach 1 is about 661 mph.
sense_groups.chinese: 在36,000到60,000英尺范围内，马赫1约为661英里/小时。

sense_groups.english: Because of the variation, it is possible for an airplane flying supersonic at high altitude to be slower than a subsonic flight at sea level.
sense_groups.chinese: 由于这种变化，在高空超音速飞行的飞机可能比海平面亚音速飞行的飞机更慢。

sense_groups.english: The transonic band (the 'sound barrier') extends from around Mach 0.8 — when the first supersonic shock waves form on the wing — to Mach 1.2, when the entire wing has gone supersonic.

questions.full:
Keith Haring began as an underground artist, literally.
His first famous projects were pieces of ______ graffiti drawn in New York subway stations.
Haring traveled from station to station, drawing with chalk and chatting with commuters about his work.
These doodles helped him develop his classic style and he ______ so prolific, doing up to 40 drawings a day, that it was not long before fame and a measure of fortune followed.

He believed that art, or at least his art, was for everyone.

sense_groups.english: Keith Haring began as an underground artist, literally.
sense_groups.chinese: 基思·哈林最初是一名地下艺术家，字面意义上的。

sense_groups.english: His first famous projects were pieces of stylized graffiti drawn in New York subway stations.
sense_groups.chinese: 他最早著名的作品是在纽约地铁站画的风格化涂鸦。

sense_groups.english: Haring traveled from station to station, drawing with chalk and chatting with commuters about his work.
sense_groups.chinese: 哈林从一个车站到另一个车站，用粉笔画画，并与通勤者聊他的作品。

sense_groups.chinese: 这些涂鸦帮助他形成了自己的经典风格，他变得非常多产，每天画多达40幅画，不久之后名声和一定的财富就随之而来。

sense_groups.english: Soon, galleries and collectors from the art establishment wanted to buy full-sized pieces by Haring.
sense_groups.chinese: 很快，艺术界的画廊和收藏家想要购买哈林的全尺寸作品。

sense_groups.english: The paintings skyrocketed in price but this did not sit well with Haring's philosophy.
sense_groups.chinese: 这些画作价格飙升，但这与哈林的理念不符。

sense_groups.english: He believed that art, or at least his art, was for everyone.
sense_groups.chinese: 他相信艺术，至少是他的艺术，是为所有人服务的。

sense_groups.english: Soon, Haring opened a store which he called the Pop Shop, which he hoped would attract a broad range of people.
sense_groups.chinese: 很快，哈林开了一家店，他称之为波普商店，希望它能吸引各种各样的人。

sense_groups.english: While somewhat controversial among street artists, some of whom accused Haring of 'selling out', the Pop Shop changed the way people thought about the relationship between art and business.
sense_groups.chinese: 虽然这在街头艺术家中有些争议，其中一些人指责哈林“出卖自己”，但波普商店改变了人们对艺术与商业关系的看法。

questions.name: #597 Marshmallow Test
questions.en:
Mischel is the creator of the marshmallow test, one of the most famous experiments in the history of psychology, which is often cited as evidence of the importance of self-control.
In the original test, which was administered at the Bing Nursery School, at Stanford, in the nineteen-sixties, Mischel's team would present a child with a treat (marshmallows were just one option) and tell her that she could either eat the one treat ______ or wait alone in the room for several minutes until the researcher returned, at which point she could have two treats.
The promised treats were always visible and the child knew that all she had to do to stop the agonizing wait was ring a bell to call the experimenter back – although in that ______ , she wouldn't get the second treat.
The longer a child delayed gratification, Mischel found – that is, the longer she was able to wait – the better she would fare later in life at numerous measures of what we now call executive function.
She would ______ better academically, earn more money, and be healthier and happier.
She would also be more likely to avoid a number of negative outcomes, including jail time, obesity, and drug use .
frequently , perform , immediately , achieve , case , topic
questions.full:
Mischel is the creator of the marshmallow test, one of the most famous experiments in the history of psychology, which is often cited as evidence of the importance of self-control.
In the original test, which was administered at the Bing Nursery School, at Stanford, in the nineteen-sixties, Mischel's team would present a child with a treat (marshmallows were just one option) and tell her that she could either eat the one treat ______ or wait alone in the room for several minutes until the researcher returned, at which point she could have two treats.
The promised treats were always visible and the child knew that all she had to do to stop the agonizing wait was ring a bell to call the experimenter back – although in that ______ , she wouldn't get the second treat.
The longer a child delayed gratification, Mischel found – that is, the longer she was able to wait – the better she would fare later in life at numerous measures of what we now call executive function.
She would ______ better academically, earn more money, and be healthier and happier.
She would also be more likely to avoid a number of negative outcomes, including jail time, obesity, and drug use .

frequently , perform , immediately , achieve , case , topic

答案:
1. immediately
2. case
3. perform

sense_groups.english: Mischel is the creator of the marshmallow test, one of the most famous experiments in the history of psychology, which is often cited as evidence of the importance of self-control.
sense_groups.chinese: 米歇尔是棉花糖测试的创始人，这是心理学史上最著名的实验之一，常被引用来证明自控力的重要性。

sense_groups.english: In the original test, which was administered at the Bing Nursery School, at Stanford, in the nineteen-sixties, Mischel's team would present a child with a treat (marshmallows were just one option) and tell her that she could either eat the one treat immediately or wait alone in the room for several minutes until the researcher returned, at which point she could have two treats.
sense_groups.chinese: 在最初的测试中，该测试于20世纪60年代在斯坦福大学的宾幼儿园进行，米歇尔的团队会给一个孩子一份零食（棉花糖只是其中一种选择），并告诉她要么立即吃掉这一份零食，要么独自在房间里等几分钟直到研究员回来，那时她可以得到两份零食。

sense_groups.english: The promised treats were always visible and the child knew that all she had to do to stop the agonizing wait was ring a bell to call the experimenter back – although in that case, she wouldn't get the second treat.
sense_groups.chinese: 承诺的零食总是可见的，孩子知道要结束痛苦的等待只需按铃叫回实验者——但在那种情况下，她不会得到第二份零食。

sense_groups.english: The longer a child delayed gratification, Mischel found – that is, the longer she was able to wait – the better she would fare later in life at numerous measures of what we now call executive function.
sense_groups.chinese: 米歇尔发现，孩子延迟满足的时间越长——也就是说，她能等待的时间越长——她在日后生活中诸多我们现在称为执行功能的指标上表现就越好。

sense_groups.english: She would perform better academically, earn more money, and be healthier and happier.
sense_groups.chinese: 她在学业上会表现更好，赚更多钱，更健康，也更快乐。

sense_groups.english: She would also be more likely to avoid a number of negative outcomes, including jail time, obesity, and drug use.
sense_groups.chinese: 她也更有可能避免许多负面结果，包括入狱、肥胖和吸毒。

A chemical incident is the uncontrolled release of a toxic substance, potentially ______ in harm to public health and the environment.
Chemical incidents can ______ as a result of natural events, or as a result of accidental or intentional events.
These incidents can be sudden and acute or have a slow ______ when there is a ‘silent’ release of a chemical.
They can also range from small releases to full-scale major ______ .
onset , categories , occur , pitch , emergencies , containing , concur , resulting
questions.full:
A chemical incident is the uncontrolled release of a toxic substance, potentially ______ in harm to public health and the environment.
Chemical incidents can ______ as a result of natural events, or as a result of accidental or intentional events.
These incidents can be sudden and acute or have a slow ______ when there is a ‘silent’ release of a chemical.
They can also range from small releases to full-scale major ______ .

onset , categories , occur , pitch , emergencies , containing , concur , resulting

答案:
1. resulting
2. occur
3. onset
4. emergencies

sense_groups.english: A chemical incident is the uncontrolled release of a toxic substance,
sense_groups.chinese: 化学事故是指有毒物质的失控释放，

sense_groups.english: potentially resulting in harm to public health and the environment.
sense_groups.chinese: 可能对公众健康和环境造成危害。

sense_groups.english: Chemical incidents can occur as a result of natural events,
sense_groups.chinese: 化学事故可能由自然事件引起，

sense_groups.english: or as a result of accidental or intentional events.
sense_groups.chinese: 或由意外或蓄意事件引起。

sense_groups.english: These incidents can be sudden and acute
sense_groups.chinese: 这些事故可能是突发性的、急性的，

sense_groups.english: or have a slow onset when there is a ‘silent’ release of a chemical.
sense_groups.chinese: 或当化学品‘无声’释放时，具有缓慢的发作过程。

sense_groups.english: They can also range from small releases to full-scale major emergencies.
sense_groups.chinese: 它们也可能从小规模泄漏到全面重大紧急情况。

questions.name: #764 Water
questions.en:

Human population growth has increased the ______ and use of water, which in turn reduced freshwater ______ in many regions, both for human consumption and for ecosystems.
covered , constantly , redundantly , edited , susceptibility , extraction , availability
questions.full:
Approximately 75% of the Earth’s surface is ______ by liquid water and ice.
Water is ______ moving between the atmosphere, land, and ocean, shaping our planet’s climate and ecosystems.
Human population growth has increased the ______ and use of water, which in turn reduced freshwater ______ in many regions, both for human consumption and for ecosystems.

covered , constantly , redundantly , edited , susceptibility , extraction , availability

答案:
1. covered
2. constantly
3. extraction
4. availability

sense_groups.english: Approximately 75% of the Earth’s surface is covered by liquid water and ice.
sense_groups.chinese: 大约75%的地球表面被液态水和冰覆盖。

sense_groups.english: Water is constantly moving between the atmosphere, land, and ocean,
sense_groups.chinese: 水在大气、陆地和海洋之间不断移动，

sense_groups.english: shaping our planet’s climate and ecosystems.
sense_groups.chinese: 塑造着地球的气候和生态系统。

sense_groups.english: Human population growth has increased the extraction and use of water,
sense_groups.chinese: 人口增长增加了水的提取和使用，

sense_groups.english: which in turn reduced freshwater availability in many regions,
sense_groups.chinese: 这反过来减少了许多地区的淡水可用性，

sense_groups.english: both for human consumption and for ecosystems.
sense_groups.chinese: 无论是对于人类消费还是生态系统。

questions.name: #765 Child Health
questions.en:
Protecting and improving the health of children is of ______ importance.
Over the past several decades, we have seen dramatic ______ in improving the health and reducing the mortality rate of young children.
However, a great deal of work ______ to further improve the health outcomes for children.
Many child deaths are due to conditions that could be easily ______ or treated given access to health care and improvements to their quality of life.
valid , fundamental , remains , progress , deduction , removed , prevented , determines
questions.full:
Protecting and improving the health of children is of ______ importance.
Over the past several decades, we have seen dramatic ______ in improving the health and reducing the mortality rate of young children.
However, a great deal of work ______ to further improve the health outcomes for children.
Many child deaths are due to conditions that could be easily ______ or treated given access to health care and improvements to their quality of life.

valid , fundamental , remains , progress , deduction , removed , prevented , determines

答案:
1. fundamental
2. progress
3. remains
4. prevented

sense_groups.english: Protecting and improving the health of children is of fundamental importance.
sense_groups.chinese: 保护和改善儿童的健康至关重要。

sense_groups.english: Over the past several decades, we have seen dramatic progress in improving the health and reducing the mortality rate of young children.
sense_groups.chinese: 在过去的几十年里，我们在改善儿童健康和降低死亡率方面取得了显著进展。

sense_groups.english: However, a great deal of work remains to further improve the health outcomes for children.
sense_groups.chinese: 然而，仍有大量工作要做，以进一步改善儿童的健康状况。

sense_groups.english: Many child deaths are due to conditions that could be easily prevented or treated given access to health care and improvements to their quality of life.
sense_groups.chinese: 许多儿童死亡是由于那些在获得医疗保健和改善生活质量的情况下本可以轻易预防或治疗的疾病造成的。

questions.name: #766 Potassium and Bone
questions.en:
A higher potassium intake has also been ______ with increased bone density and bone strength.
While researchers are ______ as to why, one theory is that potassium helps to neutralize acids that naturally occur when eating animal protein and sodium.
Without ______ potassium to neutralize these acids, calcium is pulled from the bones to do the job instead, and without enough calcium, bones become weaker.
associated , adequate , conclusive , divided , unclear , harmonious
questions.full:
A higher potassium intake has also been ______ with increased bone density and bone strength.
While researchers are ______ as to why, one theory is that potassium helps to neutralize acids that naturally occur when eating animal protein and sodium.
Without ______ potassium to neutralize these acids, calcium is pulled from the bones to do the job instead, and without enough calcium, bones become weaker.

associated , adequate , conclusive , divided , unclear , harmonious

答案:
1. associated
2. unclear
3. adequate

sense_groups.english: A higher potassium intake has also been associated with increased bone density and bone strength.
sense_groups.chinese: 较高的钾摄入量也与骨密度和骨强度的增加有关。

sense_groups.english: While researchers are unclear as to why, one theory is that potassium helps to neutralize acids that naturally occur when eating animal protein and sodium.
sense_groups.chinese: 虽然研究人员不清楚原因，但一种理论认为钾有助于中和摄入动物蛋白和钠时自然产生的酸。

sense_groups.english: Without adequate potassium to neutralize these acids, calcium is pulled from the bones to do the job instead, and without enough calcium, bones become weaker.
sense_groups.chinese: 如果没有足够的钾来中和这些酸，钙就会从骨骼中被抽出来代替完成这项工作，而如果没有足够的钙，骨骼就会变得更脆弱。

questions.name: #768 Complementary Foods
questions.en:

An infant of this age is also developmentally ready for other foods.
This transition is ______ to as complementary feeding.
If complementary foods are not introduced around the age of 6 months, or if they are given inappropriately, an infant’s growth may ______ .
required , occur , exceed , falter , referred , demand , meet
questions.full:
Around the age of 6 months, an infant's need for energy and nutrients starts to ______ what is provided by breast milk, and complementary foods are necessary to ______ those needs.
An infant of this age is also developmentally ready for other foods.
This transition is ______ to as complementary feeding.
If complementary foods are not introduced around the age of 6 months, or if they are given inappropriately, an infant’s growth may ______ .

required , occur , exceed , falter , referred , demand , meet

答案:
1. exceed
2. meet
3. referred
4. falter

sense_groups.english: Around the age of 6 months,
sense_groups.chinese: 大约在6个月大时，

sense_groups.english: an infant's need for energy and nutrients starts to exceed
sense_groups.chinese: 婴儿对能量和营养的需求开始超过

sense_groups.english: what is provided by breast milk,
sense_groups.chinese: 母乳所提供的量，

sense_groups.english: and complementary foods are necessary to meet those needs.
sense_groups.chinese: 因此需要添加辅食来满足这些需求。

sense_groups.english: An infant of this age is also developmentally ready for other foods.
sense_groups.chinese: 这个月龄的婴儿在发育上也准备好接受其他食物了。

sense_groups.english: This transition is referred to as complementary feeding.
sense_groups.chinese: 这一过渡被称为辅食喂养。

sense_groups.english: If complementary foods are not introduced around the age of 6 months,
sense_groups.chinese: 如果在6个月左右没有引入辅食，

sense_groups.english: or if they are given inappropriately,
sense_groups.chinese: 或者喂养不当，

sense_groups.english: an infant’s growth may falter.
sense_groups.chinese: 婴儿的生长发育可能会受阻。

questions.name: #769 Dementia

questions.full:
Dementia is an ______ term for several diseases affecting memory, other cognitive abilities and behavior that ______ significantly with a person’s ability to maintain their activities of daily living.
There is often a lack of awareness and understanding of dementia, resulting in stigmatization and barriers to ______ and care.

tag , interfere , diagnosis , bottom , large , unexpired , umbrella

答案:
1. umbrella
2. interfere
3. diagnosis
4. large

sense_groups.english: Dementia is an umbrella term for several diseases
sense_groups.chinese: 痴呆症是一个涵盖多种疾病的统称

sense_groups.english: affecting memory, other cognitive abilities and behavior
sense_groups.chinese: 影响记忆、其他认知能力和行为

sense_groups.english: that interfere significantly with a person’s ability
sense_groups.chinese: 这些疾病会严重干扰一个人的能力

sense_groups.english: to maintain their activities of daily living.

sense_groups.english: There is often a lack of awareness and understanding of dementia,

sense_groups.chinese: 痴呆症对护理者、家庭和整个社会的影响

questions.name: #770 Weddell Seals
questions.en:
A healthy adult Weddell seal can stay underwater for 20 minutes, and some of them even have the power to ______ for over 1 hour.
However, after giving birth, the mother seals have to ______ some of their own iron stock by transferring iron from their livers to the milk they ______ their pups so that their offspring can become better divers.
This direct transfer of iron ______ in reduced diving time for the mothers.
enhance , engages , dive , sacrifice , search , results , feed
questions.full:
A healthy adult Weddell seal can stay underwater for 20 minutes, and some of them even have the power to ______ for over 1 hour.
However, after giving birth, the mother seals have to ______ some of their own iron stock by transferring iron from their livers to the milk they ______ their pups so that their offspring can become better divers.
This direct transfer of iron ______ in reduced diving time for the mothers.

enhance , engages , dive , sacrifice , search , results , feed

答案:
1. dive
2. sacrifice
3. feed
4. results

sense_groups.english: A healthy adult Weddell seal can stay underwater for 20 minutes,
sense_groups.chinese: 一只健康的成年威德尔海豹可以在水下停留20分钟，

sense_groups.english: and some of them even have the power to dive for over 1 hour.
sense_groups.chinese: 有些甚至有能力潜水超过1小时。

sense_groups.english: However, after giving birth,
sense_groups.chinese: 然而，在分娩后，

sense_groups.english: the mother seals have to sacrifice some of their own iron stock
sense_groups.chinese: 母海豹不得不牺牲自己的一部分铁储备，

sense_groups.english: by transferring iron from their livers to the milk they feed their pups
sense_groups.chinese: 通过将铁从肝脏转移到它们喂养幼崽的奶中，

sense_groups.english: so that their offspring can become better divers.
sense_groups.chinese: 以便它们的后代能成为更好的潜水者。

sense_groups.english: This direct transfer of iron results in reduced diving time for the mothers.
sense_groups.chinese: 这种直接的铁转移导致母海豹的潜水时间减少。

Infants and toddlers cannot understand death.

2. attuned

sense_groups.english: Infants and toddlers cannot understand death.

sense_groups.english: They function in the present

questions.full:

questions.name: #775 Denial

questions.name: #862 Evolution
questions.en:
In The Origin of Species, Darwin provided abundant evidence that life on Earth has evolved over time, and he proposed natural selection as the primary mechanism for that change.
He observed that individuals ______ in their inherited traits and that selection acts on such differences, leading to ______ change.
Although Darwin realized that variation in heritable traits is a prerequisite for ______ , he did not know precisely how organisms pass heritable traits to their offspring.
Just a few years after Darwin published The Origin of Species, Gregor Mendel wrote a groundbreaking paper on inheritance in pea plants.
In that paper, Mendel proposed a model of inheritance in which organisms transmit discrete heritable units (now called genes) to their offspring.
Although Darwin did not know about genes, Mendel’s paper set the stage ______ understanding the genetic differences on which evolution is based.
form , growth , rough , differ , evolutionary , for , by , evolution
questions.full:
In The Origin of Species, Darwin provided abundant evidence that life on Earth has evolved over time, and he proposed natural selection as the primary mechanism for that change.
He observed that individuals ______ in their inherited traits and that selection acts on such differences, leading to ______ change.

2. evolutionary
3. evolution

sense_groups.english: In The Origin of Species, Darwin provided abundant evidence that life on Earth has evolved over time,
sense_groups.chinese: 在《物种起源》中，达尔文提供了大量证据，表明地球上的生命随时间进化，

sense_groups.chinese: 并提出了自然选择是这种变化的主要机制。

sense_groups.chinese: 他观察到个体在遗传特征上存在差异，

sense_groups.chinese: 并且选择作用于这些差异，导致进化性变化。

sense_groups.english: Although Darwin realized that variation in heritable traits is a prerequisite for evolution,
sense_groups.chinese: 尽管达尔文意识到遗传特征的变异是进化的前提，

sense_groups.english: he did not know precisely how organisms pass heritable traits to their offspring.
sense_groups.chinese: 但他并不确切知道生物体如何将遗传特征传递给后代。

sense_groups.english: Just a few years after Darwin published The Origin of Species,
sense_groups.chinese: 就在达尔文发表《物种起源》几年后，

sense_groups.english: Gregor Mendel wrote a groundbreaking paper on inheritance in pea plants.
sense_groups.chinese: 格雷戈尔·孟德尔写了一篇关于豌豆植物遗传的开创性论文。

sense_groups.english: in which organisms transmit discrete heritable units (now called genes) to their offspring.
sense_groups.chinese: 其中生物体将离散的遗传单位（现在称为基因）传递给后代。

sense_groups.english: Although Darwin did not know about genes,
sense_groups.chinese: 尽管达尔文不知道基因的存在，

sense_groups.english: Mendel’s paper set the stage for understanding the genetic differences on which evolution is based.
sense_groups.chinese: 但孟德尔的论文为理解进化所基于的遗传差异奠定了基础。

questions.name: #864 Pidgins

questions.full:

questions.full:
Over the last ten thousand years there seem to have been two separate and conflicting building sentiments throughout the history of towns and cities.

sense_groups.english: Over the last ten thousand years there seem to have been two separate and conflicting building sentiments throughout the history of towns and cities.
sense_groups.chinese: 在过去一万年里，城镇和城市的历史中似乎存在着两种分离且相互冲突的建设理念。

sense_groups.english: Specifically, one is the desire to start again, for a variety of reasons:
sense_groups.chinese: 具体来说，一种是出于各种原因重新开始的愿望：

sense_groups.chinese: 地震或海啸可能摧毁了定居点，或者火灾将其烧毁，

sense_groups.chinese: 已有的定居点吸引人们，他们往往会来，无论是否有任何规划他们的到来。

sense_groups.english: Incidentally, many settlements have been planned from the beginning but, for a variety of reasons, no settlement followed the plan.
sense_groups.chinese: 顺便提一下，许多定居点从一开始就有规划，但由于各种原因，没有一个定居点遵循了规划。

sense_groups.english: A good example is Currowan, on the Clyde River in New South Wales,
sense_groups.chinese: 一个很好的例子是位于新南威尔士州克莱德河畔的卡罗万，

sense_groups.english: which was surveyed in the second half of the 19th century,
sense_groups.chinese: 它在19世纪下半叶被勘测，

sense_groups.english: in expectation that people would come to establish agriculture and a small port.
sense_groups.chinese: 期望人们会来建立农业和一个小港口。

sense_groups.english: But no one came.
sense_groups.chinese: 但没有人来。
